title: Regula Systems pilot governance gate review
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on governance and security gating items for the pilot. Discussed SSO/SAML integration, audit logging mechanics, data retention policy (90 vs 180 days), SOC 2 artifacts and required controls, and next steps to validate log shipping and retention. Agreed to run a short audit-log ingestion test and share SOC2 report and architecture diagram. Customer requested formal onboarding checklist and estimated Dedicated pricing for baseline throughput.

Jordan to provide preliminary Dedicated pricing estimate for 25k tokens/day by 2026-05-16

transcript:
MEETING HEADER: 2026-05-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (CTO - Regula), Aisha Rahman (Security Architect), Ben Cho (SRE), Lina Park (Legal)

SUMMARY (auto): weekly governance gate for pilot - focus on SSO, audit logs, retention, SOC2 artifacts and next steps.

TOPICS COVERED: SSO/SAML, audit log mechanics, retention windows, KMS/encryption, SOC2 attestation, private VPC options, checklist for production gate.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. can we do quick intros? um we'll try to keep to the governance items so you have what you need to decide on the gate.
[00:18] Michael: yeah thanks jordan, quick intro from my side, i'm michael, cto at regula. we're running the pilot against our customer support flow, about 10k tokens a day right now.
[00:28] Aisha: aisha, security architect, i'm here to confirm controls - esp SSO, audit logs, retention policy.
[00:33] Ben: ben, SRE, I'll look at the operational side and do the log ingestion tests.
[00:38] Jordan: cool. priya from our side will cover technical approach for audit logs and SSO. priya go ahead.
[00:45] Priya: thanks jordan. um quick recap: we've got the pilot running on Hosted API with prefix caching enabled. for the governance gate you asked about three things: SSO, audit logs, and retention. i'll cover each at a high level and then we can drill.
[01:05] Priya: SSO - we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC. we can do IdP-initiated or SP-initiated flows, we've done okta and azure ad. we also have SCIM for user provisioning if you want RBAC. (mis-transcribed: 'Samul' sometimes in notes)
[01:24] Aisha: when you say RBAC, is that tenant-level roles or token-level roles? we need token-level separation for dev/test/prod.
[01:33] Priya: yeah, we support role scoping at token level; you can tie an API key to a workspace that maps to an IdP group. That allows dev/test/prod isolation.
[01:47] Michael: any extra effort to do SSO for our pilot team vs full org? we want to onboard 6 users only initially.
[01:54] Jordan: usually minimal, we can do a scoped app in okta in under a day. priya can share the SSO setup doc.
[02:02] Priya: i'll send the SAML metadata and sample assertion payload.
[02:08] Aisha: great. second - audit logs. we need immutable logs for requests, identity, and redaction markers. how granular are your logs?
[02:20] Priya: logs include request id, timestamp, user id, model id, token counts, and a redaction flag if PII was detected by our pipeline. you can either ship logs to our hosted retention or forward to your SIEM (splunk, sumo, or your kafka/elastic stack) via secure syslog/HTTPS.
[02:39] Ben: what's the format? json-lines? and is there an event schema?
[02:44] Priya: yes json-lines. we have an event schema spec - i'll attach it. fields: request_id, user, workspace, model_variant, input_hash (optional), tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, response_redacted (bool), and reason codes. note: kv cache references may appear as 'K V cache' in some logs.
[03:08] Aisha: retention - our baseline is 90 days for logs, but legal may request 7 year retention for some regulated data. what's your default?
[03:18] Jordan: hosted default is 90 days for full logs, 365 days for aggregated billing metrics. we can offer extended retention for an add-on or via forwarding to your storage. for private deployments you control retention fully.
[03:33] Lina: do you support on-demand export for e-discovery? we need to produce logs in response to legal requests.
[03:40] Priya: yes, exports can be generated. for hosted flows, we can provide a zipped bundle for a date range. for private/Dedicated you can run queries directly.
[03:50] Michael: SOC 2 - we need to see Type II. what's current status?
[03:55] Jordan: we have SOC 2 Type II for Redwood Inference covering the hosted control plane and processing; i'll share the report. note there's a scoping note for Dedicated/private where some controls shift to the customer.
[04:09] Aisha: can you highlight which controls shift for private deployment? encryption key management?
[04:15] Priya: yes. for Private/VPC deployments, customer manages the KMS keys and network perimeter. Redwood's attestation will note those as customer-managed. we'll flag the shared responsibility matrix.
[04:26] Ben: for the audit-log ingestion test, what's a realistic payload? I'd like to try 10k events with some 1% PII redaction markers.
[04:35] Priya: that's fine. we recommend a steady stream or batched push; we support both. we'll provide a sample generator script.
[04:45] Jordan: action - ben to run the 10k event test and share a sample set so we can validate schema and retention behavior.
[04:52] Ben: noted.
[04:55] Aisha: encryption - at rest and in transit? we need TLS + customer-managed KMS for keys.
[05:02] Priya: TLS in transit always. at rest: hosted uses provider-managed KMS by default, but we offer a customer-KMS option in Dedicated/Private where you supply key material via KMS/HSM. we'll surface the steps.
[05:18] Michael: data residency - some customers require EU-only processing. can you pin region?
[05:24] Jordan: yes, we have regional endpoints. we can route Regula traffic to eu-west-1 for the pilot; for private you can run in your cloud region.
[05:33] Lina: for compliance sign-off, we need an onboarding checklist and an evidence pack. can you put together a pack with configs, SOC2, SSO proof, and architecture diagram?
[05:42] Priya: yes, we'll produce an evidence pack. i'll include sample logs with redaction markers (sanitized).
[05:50] Jordan: anything else on retention policy? any leaning toward 90 vs 180?
[05:55] Aisha: security would prefer 180 for initial pilot so we have extra time to investigate incidents. legal may push back on cost.
[06:04] Michael: ops prefers minimal cost - can we forward to our S3 bucket to avoid Redwood retention charges?
[06:09] Priya: absolutely. we support log forwarding to your S3 with server-side encryption and lifecycle rules. that gives you indefinite retention without our add-on.
[06:20] Ben: if we forward to S3, does Redwood still keep a short-term index for search?
[06:25] Priya: we keep a 7-day index for quick queries; longer queries will hit your exported storage.
[06:32] Jordan: let's walk through the proposed timeline for the gate decision.
[06:36] Jordan: milestone A: security review complete and log test validated by 2026-05-21. milestone B: legal sign-off on evidence pack by 2026-05-24. milestone C: pricing and contract review by 2026-05-28. does that work?
[06:49] Michael: that aligns with our internal timeline.
[06:52] Lina: yes that's good. please include escalation contacts in the pack.
[06:58] Priya: noted.
[07:02] Priya: a quick note on PII redaction: our pipeline attempts token-level redaction and will attach a redaction score. it's not guaranteed to remove everything; we recommend minimizing PII in prompts.
[07:18] Aisha: can you show the redaction flag in a sample log?
[07:22] Priya: i've got a sample in the artifacts i'll attach — shows response_redacted:true and reason_code: 'email' or 'ssn'.
[07:30] Ben: when redaction occurs, do you still forward full text to S3? we want forwarded storage to be the redacted copy.
[07:36] Priya: we can configure forwarding of redacted payloads only, or raw if you choose. default hosted forwarding is redacted for compliance.
[07:47] Michael: ok good. pricing - can you ballpark Dedicated if we need reserved capacity?
[07:52] Jordan: preliminary for the capacity you mentioned (25k tokens/day and baseline latency SLO of 200ms p50) is X per month - i'll send a formal estimate. (note: price redacted in notes)
[08:04] Aisha: do you have automatic rollback or fallback if a model exceeds latency SLO? we need graceful degradation.
[08:12] Priya: yes, runtime supports routing policies - automatic fallback to cheaper model variant or to cached responses. we can set thresholds per route.
[08:22] Ben: for the log test - do you accept gzipped ndjson over HTTPS?
[08:28] Priya: yes. we'll provide an endpoint and auth token for the test.
[08:33] Jordan: quick check, any outstanding blockers from legal/security?
[08:38] Lina: we want the SOC2 report, evidence pack, and clarification on KMS responsibilities. after those are provided we'll enter the final review.
[08:47] Jordan: will do.
[08:50] Priya: i'll attach sample terraform snippets for VPC peering and security group rules so Ben can iterate quickly.
[08:58] Ben: love that.
[09:00] Jordan: ok let's confirm owners again: Jordan - SOC2 and pricing; Priya - architecture, logs schema, terraform snippets; Ben - run ingestion test and share results; Lina - legal list and timeline.
[09:16] Michael: fine by me.
[09:20] Jordan: any other q's?
[09:23] Aisha: one small one - do you capture prompt history for model training? our privacy team is nervous about reuse.
[09:29] Priya: by default we do not use customer prompts to train public models; there's a setting to opt-in for research only. we can provide the policy statement.
[09:39] Lina: please include that statement in the evidence pack.
[09:42] Jordan: will do.
[09:45] Priya: last thing - i'll schedule the deeper technical session with Ben and the infra folks for next tuesday (2026-05-19).
[09:53] Ben: that's good for me.
[09:55] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and next steps.
[10:00] Meeting ended.

ACTION ITEMS (auto): Jordan: send SOC2 and pricing; Priya: architecture and logs schema; Ben: ingestion test; Lina: compile legal exceptions.

ATTACHMENTS MENTIONED: SSO setup doc (SAML metadata), audit-log schema (ndjson spec), sample terraform for VPC peering, SOC2 attestation (to be shared), sample redaction logs (sanitized).

NOTES ABOUT TRANSCRIPTION: occasional mis-hearings: 'SAML' appears as 'Samul' in autogenerated captions; 'KV cache' sometimes split as 'K V cache'.
